fix: 'Culms solitary' means one stem per plant. Moving the value to the whole plant changes it to 'the plant grows alone'. Keep culm as stem (PO_0009047). 'tufted' (caespitose) can stay on the whole plant.
reason: 'solitary' is said of the culms, not of the plant. 'Whole plant solitary' says something else (plants not growing in groups).
The base of the leaf blade is cuneate.

fix: Better: add the pistillate (female, PATO_0000383) slot. 'Solitary' holds only for pistillate flowers. Staminate flowers are in fascicles of 2–20.
reason: The choice 'solitary or fascicled' is true of the flowers of this taxon. Dropping 'pistillate' loses detail but does not make the statement false.
'later' (after flowering) is fairly read as the mature state. The leaf-blade surfaces become glabrous.

target: plant cell wall (GO_0009505), part of basal laminal cells
fix: 'cells … walls thin' means the wall is thin, not the cell. Make the wall the bearer, inside the cell. Also keep the position ('basal'): the distal cells' walls are 'thin to irregularly thickened'.
reason: Thinness is said of the cell walls of the basal laminal cells, not of the whole cell.
'Arbre de 10 m de haut': the tree is 10 m tall.

fix: 'Filaments …' should map to the filament, not the whole stamen.
reason: 'subequal' is said of the filaments (median pairs 3.5–5 mm, lateral pair 3–4.5 mm), not of the whole stamens.

target: 2–7 mm for all pedicels; up to 12 mm in female flowers
fix: In 'A–B(–C in X)', the extreme C applies only to X. Make one annotation of A–B with no context, and another of up to C (lower end unknown) with the X context. Do not join them into A–C with X as the whole.
reason: The flora gives 2–7 mm in general and up to 12 mm only for pedicels of female flowers. The annotation joins these into 2–12 mm, all in female flowers.
Bracts are smaller than the leaves.
The leaflets are hairy on the lower (abaxial) side. Mapping that to the leaf's abaxial epidermis is acceptable. 'loosely appressed' is just a detail that was dropped.
The leaves are longer than the culm (stem).

fix: Strictly, the bearer is the stigma lobes. Using the stigma is acceptable.
reason: The lobes of the 3-fid stigma are recurved at anthesis. The flowering-stage context is right.
'black-gray' is a dark gray. Gray is the base color.
The perianth segments of Atriplex are tepals. 'linear-oblong' is a kind of oblong.

fix: 'N-several' / 'N-many' means at least N with an open upper end. Do not read it as exactly N–N.
reason: '2-several seeds' does not mean exactly 2 seeds.
The leaf margin is entire.
1–3 seeds per capsule.

fix: The word 'apex' inside the from-text was not turned into the bearer. 'apex X to Y' should give the leaf apex as the bearer, as it does for single values.
reason: Acute to acuminate is said of the leaf apex, not the whole leaf.

fix: Nerve counts given after the calyx teeth describe the whole calyx. Put the container at the calyx level, not one sepal. The '±' (approximately) qualifier is also missing.
reason: About 15 nerves are given for the whole calyx (a tube divided into teeth), not for each sepal.

fix: In sedges (Carex), 'staminate spike' vs 'pistillate spike' must keep the sex in the state slot. The stalk and position of the two kinds of spike differ.
reason: Only the staminate spike is short-stalked or nearly sessile. Pistillate spikes in Carex are often longer-stalked.
The bark is reddish.
Petals are spatulate or obovate.

target: pedicel of female flower (whole: flower + female PATO_0000383)
fix: After a sentence opening 'Female flowers …;', the parts that follow belong to the female flower until a new sex heading. Carry the sex over as the whole/state slot.
reason: The 2–4 cm pedicels are those of the female flowers. Male flowers are described separately before this.

fix: In '<color> central vein', the color belongs to the vein (midvein). It should not be moved up to the leaf.
reason: Only the central vein is pinkish. The leaf itself is green.
The raceme often has 2–6 flowers.
The inflorescences have many flowers. 'rather' only softens 'many'.
The involucral bracts are acutish, that is, subacute.
The spikelets are never proliferous. The negation is right.
The leaves are numerous.
The basal leaves form a rosette. The 'basal' context is right.
